about: Calibration rules for the Cyber Risk in Dollars report. Every weight, threshold and loss figure here is a Fluency proposal for a mid-market organization and is listed in references/calibration_rules.md. Change this file, then run scripts/make_calibration_doc.py.

benchmarks.as_of: IBM Cost of a Data Breach 2025 and FBI IC3
benchmarks.text: IBM Cost of a Data Breach 2025: global average breach $4.44M, US average $10.22M, ransomware or extortion incident $5.08M, shadow AI adds about $670K. FBI IC3: BEC loss per complaint roughly $130K. Verify with a web search when more than a year old.

ransomware.name: Ransomware & operational extortion
ransomware.description: Encryption of servers and endpoints, with possible data theft, halting operations.

factors.label: anti-ransomware hardening not confirmed

factors.label: EDR agents not in Protect mode

factors.label: CrowdStrike sensors with reduced protection

factors.label: aging exploitable vulnerabilities

factors.label: administrators without enforced MFA

No endpoint application inventory, so backup software exposure is unknown
No Windows audit archive, so log clearing and persistence are unknown

ransomware.anchor: Per-event cost is anchored to the IBM 2025 average cost of a ransomware or extortion incident ($5.08M) and scaled to organization size.

Forwarding changes are not in the archive (the archived script predates the counter)

bec.anchor: Per-event loss uses the FBI IC3 average BEC loss (about $130K) with a long tail for large wires.

factors.label: single-factor sign-ins

factors.label: no all-users MFA

factors.label: privileged roles exempt from MFA

breach.anchor: Per-event cost sits below the IBM 2025 global average breach ($4.44M) at mid-market scale, with a tail toward the US average ($10.22M).

exposure.name: Accidental & insider data exposure
exposure.description: Sensitive data leaves through sharing, forwarding, bulk download or an AI service by mistake or by an insider, without an external attacker.

tiers.text: All {d.matches.total} DLP matches came from rules in test mode: they are logged, not blocked
Fewer than half of DLP matches came from rules in enforce mode
Over 30% as many DLP undo events as matches, not counting edited documents (matches released or marked false positive)
At least 10% as many DLP undo events as matches, not counting edited documents (matches released or marked false positive)

factors.label: sensitive data reaching the Copilot assistant

tiers.text: {d.ai.unenforced_hits} Microsoft 365 Copilot DLP rule hits were not enforced
{d.matches.total} DLP matches in the window, at least 1 per 100 accounts
{d.matches.total} DLP matches in the window, at least 1 per 500 accounts

factors.label: DLP rules that users can override

tiers.text: DLP rule changes in the window that allow users to override the policy tip: {d.policy_config.rules_allow_override}
{d.sharing.anonymous_links_created} anonymous sharing links created in the window, at least 1 per 20 accounts
{d.sharing.anonymous_links_created} anonymous sharing links created in the window, at least 1 per 100 accounts

gaps.text: DLP shows signals from policies that matched; data that left through a path with no policy or no monitoring cannot be seen

Policy inventory, overrides with a justification, bulk downloads and web or AI egress are not in the DLP report; policy configuration covers only policies created or changed in the window, so a workload with no matches may have no policy

exposure.anchor: Per-event cost sits below the cloud breach scenario because no attacker persists in the environment; the tail reflects IBM 2025 reporting that shadow AI adds about $670K to a breach.

not_modelled.text: Accidental and insider data exposure, including shadow AI, is not modelled: the Office 365 archive counts sharing and external-access events but shows zero DLP matches, which cannot separate "no DLP policy" from "no matches", and there is no generative-AI egress source. This scenario is modelled only when the DLP report shows matches.
Third-party and remote-tool compromise is not modelled separately to avoid double counting; extra remote-access tools already raise the ransomware frequency.

treatments.name: Patch and isolate backup servers; immutable copies
treatments.detail: Upgrade the backup software to a fixed build, move backup servers out of the production domain and keep an immutable or offline copy.

treatments.name: Prove recovery: restore test and backup monitoring
treatments.detail: Run and record a restore test of the critical systems and send backup job results to the SIEM so recovery ability can be measured.

treatments.name: Close endpoint gaps and turn on anti-ransomware hardening
treatments.detail: EDR on the {r.unprotected.not_in_edr_agent_list} unprotected devices, Protect mode on every agent, ASR rules, LAPS and Credential Guard.

treatments.name: Contain active threats now
treatments.detail: Isolate infected devices and triage unresolved or unmitigated threats, starting with credential access and lateral movement.

treatments.name: Patch exploitable vulnerabilities, oldest first
treatments.detail: Close the {r.vulnerabilities.exploitable_older_than_30d_devices} devices with exploitable vulnerabilities older than 30 days.

treatments.name: Enforce MFA and Conditional Access
treatments.detail: Enforce MFA for every administrator and every user, remove role exclusions and move toward phishing-resistant methods.

treatments.name: Block legacy authentication
treatments.detail: Block legacy authentication for all users and apps with a short, reviewed exception list.

treatments.name: Payment verification and inbox-rule alerting
treatments.detail: Out-of-band verification for bank-detail changes; alert on new forwarding and inbox rules. Confirm whether this is already in place.

treatments.name: Stop log clearing; keep 90-day log retention
treatments.detail: Archive instead of clear; forward all domain-controller events to the SIEM.

treatments.name: Move DLP rules from test to enforce; enforce the Copilot policy
treatments.detail: Tune the test-mode DLP rules and enforce them on mail, files and chat; enforce the Microsoft 365 Copilot DLP policy and review the information types involved.
